text.p: Bonds could pick up pace again on Thursday providing the Treasuries remain strong but eyes will be on key U.S. economic data, traders said.
Thursday sees the release of GDP and jobless claims figures.

"With the Treasuries gaining, there are good prospects for the European market tomorrow. But things are going to be heavily conditioned by the impact of the U.S. GDP and jobless claims," said one trader.

Another trader noted that the peripheries had faced some difficulty in keeping up with the Bunds on Thursday because they "ran out of gas". But he added that the slowdown had been accompanied by a dropping off in volume. "Not many sellers appeared," he said.
The continuing lack of liquidity at the short end is tightening the spread between the two and the 10 year bonds.
